sources.requirements:
稿件要求

sources.title: 中国会计学会管理会计专业委员会2026年学术年会征文启事
sources.scope:
一、会议主题与核心议题
本次年会主题为“‘十五五’新征程：管理会计赋能新质生产力的价值创造机制与制度创新”。年会旨在搭建“政策解读—理论前沿—最佳实践—技术赋能”四位一体的高端交流平台，聚焦管理会计在新时代背景下的价值创造机制与制度创新。围绕会议主题，征文方向包括但不限于以下五个核心聚焦点及其具体子方向：
（一）数智化与管理会计转型
财务共享中心向企业数据中枢演进的路径与机制研究
人工智能在预算预测、成本控制与风险监控中的应用研究
穿透式监管背景下企业数据标准与管理会计数智化体系建设
数据同源、标准统一、互联互通的管理会计信息系统构建
企业管理会计数智化转型的成熟度评价与绩效影响研究
（二）自主知识体系与产教融合
中国自主管理会计知识体系的理论基础与框架构建研究
基于“两个结合”的管理会计哲学基础与方法论创新
管理会计教材建设与案例库开发：自主知识体系的载体研究
“政、产、学、研、用”深度融合的管理会计人才培养模式创新
中国管理会计自主知识体系的国际化路径与国际比较研究
（三）新质生产力与未来产业
sources.requirements:
二、征文要求
1. 应征论文须为未公开发表的学术论文或实务案例研究，字数原则上不超过20000字（含参考文献、附录等）。
2. 论文内容应突出学术性、创新性、实践性，鼓励基于真实案例、调研数据或政策分析的各类方法下的研究。
3. 所有应征论文视为向《会计研究》投稿，作者应确保论文为非公开发表原创作品，并未向其他任何期刊投稿。论文格式请参考《会计研究》的投稿规范，包括：题目、摘要、关键词、正文、参考文献、作者信息（姓名、单位、职称、联系方式）等。
4. 注意事项
（1）征文截止日期：2026年10月20日（以电子邮件发送时间为准）。
（2）投稿方式：请将论文电子版（Word和PDF格式）发送至会议专用邮箱：heyq@mail.nai.edu.cn，邮件主题请注明“2026管理会计年会征文+第一作者姓名+单位”。
（3）被会议录用的论文将收录到会议论文集（内部资料，不对外发布），并择优推荐至《会计研究》，如作者不同意收录，请在应征论文上注明。
5. 会议优先面向中国会计学会会员。
sources.dateText: 征文截止日期：2026年10月20日（以电子邮件发送时间为准）。

sources.title: 《信息资源管理学报》2026年重点选题领域

sources.title: 【专刊征文】《外国经济与管理》“科技创新与产业创新融合下的家族企业高质量发展”专刊征稿启事
sources.scope:
一、选题内容
本次专题征稿内容包括但不限于以下议题：
1. 家族企业在科技创新与产业创新深度融合中具有怎样的独特性？家族控制、长期导向、产业积累和传承使命如何影响企业对科技创新机会的识别、评价与转化？
2. 深厚的产业根基是家族企业推动科技创新的资源基础，还是导致路径依赖和创新惯性的诱因？家族企业如何将行业经验、客户关系、制造能力和供应链资源转化为技术创新与产业升级优势？
3. 科技创新如何嵌入家族企业的产业场景，并进一步转化为产品升级、工艺改造、商业模式更新和产业价值创造？
4. 家族控制、家族治理结构和家族成员参与如何影响企业对外部技术、创新人才、产学研合作和开放式创新的接受程度？
5. 家族企业如何在保持控制权、维护家族价值与推动突破性创新、关键技术攻关和高不确定性科技投入之间取得平衡？
6. 一代企业家、新生代接班人与代际共治如何影响家族企业的技术选择、数字化转型、科技创业和产业升级路径？
7. 职业经理人、外部专家、高端创新人才和技术团队如何参与家族企业科技创新与产业升级？家族企业如何通过授权、激励与信任机制激活外部专业力量？
8.
sources.requirements:
二、投稿要求
1. 稿件类别包括理论研究、实证研究、案例研究和文献研究。实证研究论文可以采用定性、定量、QCA、文本分析、大语言模型等方法，欢迎跨学科的交叉研究。
2. 论文应围绕“科技创新与产业创新融合下的家族企业高质量发展”主题展开，具有明确的问题意识、理论贡献或实践启示；尤其欢迎立足中国家族企业实践、回应中国民营经济高质量发展现实问题、具有本土理论创新潜力的研究。
3. 投稿论文应为未公开发表的原创性研究成果，不存在一稿多投、学术不端或知识产权争议。
4. 稿件字数为15000~20000字。
5. 稿件格式体例请参考《外国经济与管理》近期刊文格式。
6. 请在线提交稿件，并请注明“科技创新与产业创新融合下的家族企业高质量发展”专刊稿件。

sources.title: 《审计与经济研究》《南京审计大学学报》 “深入学习贯彻党的二十届四中全会精神”专栏征稿启事

sources.requirements:

2. 正文字数 8000~15000 字。

sources.title: 《心理学报》征稿启事 | 以AI为镜：数智时代的不确定性、信息特征与判断决策
sources.scope:
专刊主题与内容
本次专刊的主题为 “数智时代的信息特点、信息行为与判断决策”，涵盖（但不限于）以下研究方向：
1. 数智时代的不确定性、信息特征与认知加工特点
2. 比较AI理性与人性，开发心理学版的图灵测试, 为大语言模型提供人性基准
3. 算法推荐下的信息行为
4. 数智环境下的判断与决策偏差
5. AIGC信息的认知、信任与伦理
6. 信息韧性与数字素养
7. 人机协同决策的心理机制
8. 组织情境下的数智信息行为
9. 公共卫生与风险领域的数智环境决策
10．利用AI开发具有陪伴和干预功能的心理软件，赋能留守儿童和老年群体
sources.requirements:
收稿形式与评审流程：专刊将采用约稿与公开征稿相结合的方式，广泛征集相关领域的高质量稿件。所有稿件均需遵循《心理学报》投稿指南，并通过心理学报投稿系统（https://journal.psych.ac.cn/xlxb/CN/0439-755X/home.shtml）投稿，在文题后面的括号里注明“数智决策专刊”。所有稿件都按正常的审稿程序，实行匿名评审，确保稿件的质量和学术水平。
论文类型：我们特别鼓励多元化的研究方法，包括但不限于严格控制的实验室实验、高生态效度的实地研究、大数据分析、计算建模、神经科学方法（如脑电、fMRI）以及追踪研究等。

sources.scope:

sources.requirements:
六、征文要求
（1）坚持正确的政治方向，聚焦重大管理实践现实需求和国际学术前沿动态，研究成果须具有学术和实践价值。
（2）论文应具有原创性，未在其他学术会议、论文集和刊物上公开发表过。作者相关信息（如姓名、工作单位、通信地址、联系电话、电子信箱等）请列于独立于正文的首页。
（3）请同时提交一份论文梗概（约500—800字），内容包括研究背景、研究方法、要点结果与贡献，用于论文快速评审选择。
（4）投稿论文经快速评审选择后，将分为“分组报告论文（A类）”和“展板展示论文（B类）”推荐为会议的核心入选论文。对于A类入选论文（且排位于全部投稿前15%），在经过编委/专家点评研讨及相应修改之后，可进入《管理科学学报》的快速评审通道。
（5）稿件请使用Word格式提交，参照《管理科学学报》的撰稿格式。本次会议暂定仅接收中文论文。
（6）投稿请以“数智管理工作坊+作者姓名+单位+论文题目”作为邮件标题和文件名称，发送至邮箱：wangwei2020@zzu.edu.cn
（7）征文联系人：王巍老师；联系方式：18392071989。

sources.title: 《系统工程学报》专辑征稿启事 AI 与大数据驱动的新商业模式与供应链系统工程研究
sources.scope:
二、征稿范围
本专辑重点欢迎但不限于以下方向。投稿应突出AI、大数据、数据要素、智能体、平台算法、数字供应链、韧性安全与可持续运营等新兴研究要素，避免对成熟议题作简单变量扩展。
1. AI与大数据驱动的供应链智能决策
l AI控制塔、需求预测、采购协同、库存优化、仓网调配与履约决策。
l 预测性AI、规范性AI和强化学习在风险量化、产能配置与资源调度中的应用。
l 面向供应商网络和产业链生态的网络化规划、动态协同与资源共享机制。
2. 智能体AI与人机协同运营系统
l 智能体AI在供应链编排、平台治理、服务运营和异常处置中的主动监测与协同决策。
l 人机协同下的信任形成、责任分配、算法解释、模型幻觉控制和失效诊断。
l 企业AI落地过程中的流程重构、组织采纳与管理价值评估。
3. AI原生平台经济与新商业模式运营
l AI推荐、搜索排序、内容生成、智能客服和算法定价对平台生态与消费者行为的影响。
l 内容电商、即时零售、工业品平台、跨境平台和服务平台中的数据共享、契约设计与激励机制。
sources.requirements:
四、稿件要求及注意事项
1. 稿件应为未公开发表的原创性研究成果，主题需与本专辑方向高度相关，具有创新性、系统性和较高学术价值。
2. 论文撰写须符合《系统工程学报》的学术规范与排版要求，具体请参见期刊官方网站投稿指南。
3. 投稿时请在稿件标题前注明【AI与大数据专辑】，并在在线投稿系统中选择对应专辑栏目。投稿网站：http://jse.tju.edu.cn。
4. 所有稿件将按照《系统工程学报》审稿标准进行严格的双盲同行评议。

sources.scope: Business schools around the world are undergoing rapid transformation, reflecting questions about their social license (Starkey & Tempest, 2025; University Chancellors Council, 2025), legitimacy and identity (Alajoutsijärvi et al., 2015), changing student demographics (Zhang et al., 2016), technological developments (Clegg & Sarker, 2024; Hughes & Davis, 2024), and evolving understandings of social justice, equity, inclusion, and belonging (Fiset et al., 2025).

Submission types
For this special issue, we invite submissions to all of the Academy of Management Learning & Education’s peer-reviewed sections, including Research and Reviews, Essays, and Book and Resource Reviews. We particularly welcome research studies based on extensive data—qualitative, quantitative, and mixed method—using any well-executed and rigorous methodology and strong theoretical framing. Finally, related to the issue of representation, we especially encourage submissions from neurodivergent authors and author teams. Submissions will be subject to the normal editorial decision-making and peer-review processes. All the journal’s standard formatting and peer review guidelines will apply.
Submission details
We invite special issue submissions to occur between 1 November 2026 and 14 December 2026 through the AMLE’s manuscript central system.
Prior to submission, we will hold an optional virtual professional development workshop at the end of May 2026, for interested authors to receive feedback on their ideas. Those interested in participating in the workshop should e-mail a 3,000-word proposal (including references) to Miriam Moeller and Dana L. Ott by 13 May 2026.
We also plan to offer workshops to discuss this special issue at the European Academy of Management in June 2026 (Kristiansand, Norway), the European Group of Organisational Studies in July (Bergamo, Italy), the Academy of International Business conference in July 2026 (Manchester, UK), the Academy of Management conference in August 2026 (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) and the Brazilian Academy of Management in October 2026. We will share more details about these and other opportunities when available via the AMLE website and various listservs.
While we encourage interested contributors to participate in these opportunities, they are not a prerequisite for, or a guarantee of, eventual acceptance in the special issue.

sources.scope: Hope is situated between what is and what might be. As such, hope is typically experienced under conditions of uncertainty, and there is no paucity of uncertainty in these times of geo-political upheaval and existential threats posed by climate change.
sources.requirements:
AMLE Editors
* Katrin Muehlfeld, Trier University (Germany)

* Stuart Middleton,University of Queensland (Australia)
* Todd Bridgman,Victoria University of Wellington (New Zealand)

Call for Papers
Hope is situated between what is and what might be. As such, hope is typically experienced under conditions of uncertainty, and there is no paucity of uncertainty in these times of geo-political upheaval and existential threats posed by climate change. Why and how should/can we hope in these troubling times? This is the guiding question for us in this special section. Hope is defined as “the perceived capability to derive pathways to desired goals, and motivate oneself via agency thinking to use those pathways” (Snyder, 2002, p. 249).

sources.scope: Amid rising concern about the relevance of their contents, many scholarly journals mandate inclusion of a managerial implications section. This section may be relegated to a few paragraphs at the end of an article and comprised of speculative statements loosely connected to the paper’s empirical or theoretical content.
sources.requirements:
To highlight and enhance the process of knowledge production across AOM’s portfolio of interdependent journals and to make its scope more manageable, this special issue is limited to papers that analyze practice and policy implications previously published in any of the seven established AOM journals: Academy of Management Annals (Annals), Academy of Management Collections (Collections), Academy of Management Discoveries (AMD), Academy of Management Journal (AMJ), *Academy of Management Learning & Education*(AMLE), Academy of Management Review (AMR), and Academy of Management Perspectives (AMP).
Submissions must conduct novel empirical or conceptual analysis. AMP does not accept managerial “translations” that restate previously published work in more practice-friendly terms. Moreover, we do not accept papers that address managerial implications for which actionable solutions have already been adequately developed through prior publications. Authors submitting to this special issue may be, but are not required to be, an author of the published article containing the managerial implication.

sources.scope: ATTENTION! Please disengage the autopilot. Check the muscle memory. We do not want more of the same. Academy of Management Perspectives (AMP)is different.
sources.requirements:
If your paper is theory driven, it is NOT suited to AMP. AMP is a journal of first choice for papers that inform managerial practice and policy. We are not a backstop for papers that miss at AMJ, AMR, or other top theory-driven journals. It’s not enough to add managerial implications onto a paper rejected at such journals. AMP papers must be managerially driven from the start.
While relevance is our most prominent characteristic, it does not come at the expense of rigor. AMP does NOT publish papers that lack rigorous original analysis. Though our mission differs, our analytical standards are the same as those of other elite journals. Opinions, overviews, descriptive arguments, philosophical treatise, etc. are not within our purview, even if they convey interesting perspectives on management. The managers who rely on AMP content need evidence, not conjecture. So, the claims of an AMP paper must be supported with stringent scholarly analysis.

sources.scope: Image The newest journal of the American Economic Association, American Economic Review: Insights, invites submissions.
sources.requirements:
Papers in economics have grown substantially in length over the last four decades, leaving little scope to publish the important paper whose central contribution can be concisely presented. Yet, sometimes the most important findings are those that require little room. Paul Samuelson's landmark paper on the efficient provision of public goods was only three pages in the 1954 Review of Economics and Statistics.
AER: Insights will target the turnaround times of the most efficient journals in our profession––with an aim to get all first responses within three months at most. sources.dateText:
Antipode occasionally publishes special issues and symposia (see here and here , for some examples). The Editorial Collective seeks papers that both individually and collectively make a significant contribution to the advancement of radical/critical geography, whether by pushing debates forward in novel ways or by taking discussions in new directions. We look for papers that speak to ongoing conversations in the field, to be sure, but as representatives of an undisciplined discipline we also look for papers that stray beyond established borders (of all kinds) and that think creatively about the journal’s lines of descent and possible futures. And a “symposium”, of course, is a party, so we look for papers that are not only lively and well-presented but also engaging – papers that are in dialogue, meaningfully connecting with each other, and holding together as a collection to form something more than the sum of its parts. A strong introduction to a special issue or symposium takes on these provocations in bold and compelling ways.
Proposals should be e-mailed to Andy Kent (antipode@live.co.uk) before the end of May and October, and decisions will made before the end of June and November. If you have a question, please get in touch with Andy.

sources.title: Call for Papers (for prospective authors)
sources.scope: The Brookings Papers on Economic Activity (BPEA) is a semi-annual academic conference and journal that pairs rigorous research with policy analysis to address urgent economic challenges of the day. BPEA emphasizes rigorous analysis that has an empirical orientation, takes real-world institutions seriously, and is relevant to economic policy.
sources.requirements:
Although most BPEA papers are solicited by editors, unsolicited proposals are welcome. Interested authors should submit the following materials via the submission form below.
* Proposal:
* a completed draft paper OR
* a detailed paper outline (no more than five double-spaced pages) with specified data sources and preliminary empirical results.
* Letter to editors: A one-page letter outlining the proposal.
Editors evaluate the proposals on a rolling basis based on their originality, analytical rigor, policy relevance, and the needs of the conference program. Editorial decisions are typically made nine months prior to each conference – proposals received by December 1 are considered for the following fall conference, and those received by June 1 for the spring.
Certain proposals may be considered for conferences outside of the normal evaluation timeline, depending on the timeliness of the topics and the program needs. Proposals from early career researchers and members of underrepresented groups in the economics profession are encouraged. Given the volume of proposals we receive, only the authors of accepted proposals will be contacted, typically within three weeks.

Medicine is being reshaped by rapid digital transformation powered by expanding clinical data and fast-moving computational methods. This Article Collection, “Computational Frontiers in Medical Diagnosis and Data Analysis,” highlights research at the intersection of algorithmic innovation and clinical decision-making.
This topic matters because diagnostic decisions are high-stakes, time-sensitive, and increasingly data-intensive. Clinicians must interpret heterogeneous information—images, laboratory values, clinical notes, wearable signals, and histories—often under uncertainty and workflow pressure. Traditional approaches, though indispensable, can be limited by human bandwidth and the complexity of modern datasets.

sources.title: Call for Papers for Special Issue - “Decisions in the Agentic Era: Toward Agent-Native Decision Science”
sources.scope: Artificial intelligence is entering a new era. AI systems are no longer simply responding to instructions or providing recommendations.
sources.dateText:
Artificial intelligence is entering a new era. AI systems are no longer simply responding to instructions or providing recommendations. Increasingly, they act as agents, initiating multi-step workflows, using tools, coordinating with other agents, and making decisions with meaningful autonomy in organizational and market environments. This transformation raises a fundamental question for decision science: What happens to decision-making when the decision-maker is increasingly an AI agent?
To address this question, Decision Sciences invites submissions for a special issue titled: Decisions in the Agentic Era: Toward Agent-Native Decision Science
The special issue has two complementary objectives. First, it seeks to advance rigorous understanding of how agentic AI is reshaping decisions, markets, organizations, and society. Second, it aims to develop new research practices that enable future AI agents to reconstruct, replicate, evaluate, and extend scientific research while maintaining the standards of rigorous scholarship.
The agentic era is not simply introducing a new technology. It is changing who or what makes decisions, how decisions are made, and potentially how scientific knowledge itself is created and accumulated. We look forward to your submissions to Decision Sciences.

sources.scope: Corporate purpose has become a central theme in contemporary management scholarship (Chua et al., 2024; George et al., 2023).

sources.dateText:

Importantly, these governance innovations do more than signal intent. They are established to guide and govern reliable decision-making within corporations, structuring managerial judgment in a consistent and accountable manner under conditions of complexity and uncertainty. In this sense, they directly influence how purpose is interpreted, prioritized, and enacted in everyday managerial practice.
How do legal and organizational governance innovations embed, protect, and enforce corporate purpose? What mechanisms – such as ownership structures, board designs, mission locks, stakeholder rights, or accountability and reporting regimes – are employed, and how do they shape managerial decision-making, innovation, and long-term orientation?

sources.scope: In recent years, the remarkable progress in computer application technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data, Large Models, Blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing, 5G, and Digital Twins, has deepened their integration across various industries.
sources.dateText:
Submission deadline: Thursday, 20 August 2026
In recent years, the remarkable progress in computer application technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Big Data, Large Models, Blockchain, the Internet of Things (IoT), Cloud Computing, 5G, and Digital Twins, has deepened their integration across various industries.
The purpose of this Special Issue is to showcase the latest developments, opportunities, and applications of advanced computer applications.
We invite the submission of high-quality papers from both academia and industry that address the technical challenges and harness the potential of intelligent methods in application of computer science and encourage the submission of original research articles and comprehensive review papers that explore all aspects of this interdisciplinary field, aiming to solve existing problems and pave the way for future innovations.
We invite the submission of high-quality papers from both academia and industry that address the technical challenges and harness the potential of intelligent methods in application of computer science and encourage the submission of original research articles and comprehensive review papers that explore all aspects of this interdisciplinary field, aiming to solve existing problems and pave the way for future innovations.
The primary objective of this Call for Papers is to assess the current state-of-the-art in addressing these complex interoperability challenges through advanced computer application technologies, identify knowledge gaps, and propose future research directions. This initiative seeks to foster a comprehensive understanding of how AI, Big Data, and other emerging technologies can be leveraged to build robust, interconnected systems across diverse landscapes including industry and transportation.
We envision that the collective insights and collaborative efforts showcased at this conference will inspire and guide future innovations, ultimately leading to the advancement of both computer application technologies and the traditional engineering disciplines they seek to transform.
Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Data Science; Internet of Things (IoT); Cybersecurity; Smart Systems/Applications; Computer Applications

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: 6G-Technology-Driven Healthcare Informatics
sources.scope: The special issue on “6G-Technology-Driven Healthcare Informatics” invites pioneering research that leverages 6G communication technologies to enhance biomedical and health informatics.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Advanced Wireless Networks for Healthcare 5.0
sources.scope: Healthcare is undergoing a transformative transition toward Healthcare 5.0, a paradigm that integrates human-centric intelligence, interoperability, and continuous personalized care. At the foundation of this transition lies a new generation of advanced wireless networks, capable of enabling seamless data acquisition, real-time communication, remote monitoring, and autonomous medical decision support.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Agentic AI for Healthcare: Towards Autonomous, Trustworthy, and Human-Centric Systems
sources.scope: This Special Issue will explore Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Healthcare , focusing on systems that move beyond prediction and assistance to proactive, autonomous, and goal-directed actions under human-defined constraints.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: AI-based Solutions for Dietary Assessment: Tackling Accuracy, Efficiency, and Personalization Challenges
sources.scope: The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in food analysis offers significant potential across applications like food recognition, dietary assessment, and precision nutrition. By providing insights into the relationship between diet and non-communicable diseases (NCDs), AI contributes to disease prevention through improved eating habits.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Applying Federated Machine Learning Approaches for Human-Robot-Interaction
sources.scope: Human-robot communication, abbreviated as HRI, is the study of efficient and effective communication or interplay between humans and robots. HRI is a multidisciplinary idea usually utilized in areas including natural language processing, smart computer vision, robotics systems, artificial intelligence, and psychological studies.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: BHI 2026 Conference-Associated Call on “Intelligent Informatics for Personalized Healthcare
sources.scope: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), biomedical informatics, and computational modeling are accelerating the shift toward personalized healthcare by enabling the integration of multimodal data from genomics, medical imaging, wearable sensors, and electronic health records.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Emerging AI Paradigms for Next-Generation Medicine: Safety and Reliability in Vision-Language Models, Agentic Systems, and Digital Twins
sources.scope: AI is transforming medicine by enabling advanced diagnosis, prognosis, and personalized care. Advances in multimodal learning, foundation models, and high-performance computing allow integration of diverse medical data into unified clinical intelligence.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Computation in the Learning of Human Physiological Systems
sources.scope: This Special Issue calls for work that integrates XAI with deep learning in physiology, prioritizing studies that: 1) Develop novel interpretability techniques tailored to physiological time-series data, 2) Validate model explanations against domain knowledge (e.g., through clinician-in-the-loop evaluations), or 3) Use XAI to derive testable biological hypotheses.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Federated Learning and Digital Twins for Smart Healthcare
sources.scope: The integration of Digital Twins (DTs) and Federated Learning (FL) has tremendous potential to transform the smart healthcare sector by providing various healthcare solutions, including realtime, intelligent, personalized, and privacy-preserving healthcare services.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Generative and Agentic IoT Systems for Intelligent Digital Healthcare
sources.scope: This Special Issue explores the convergence of Generative AI and Agentic IoT (AgIoT) in next-generation digital healthcare systems. As healthcare systems face rising demands due to aging populations, chronic diseases, and limited resources, emerging GIoT/AgIoT paradigms offer transformative solutions.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Integrating Imaging with Personalized Cardiovascular Medicine: Current Advances and Future Directions
sources.scope: This Special Issue invites contributions that address aspects included in this entire pipeline: from image acquisition and processing to model development, validation, and clinical translation – all targeting improved cardiovascular insights.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Knowledge Graphs and Multimodal Data Fusion in Biomedical Informatics
sources.scope: Biomedical AI is rapidly shifting toward integrative, interpretable, and knowledge-guided intelligence as healthcare increasingly relies on heterogeneous data sources such as imaging, genomics, wearables, EHRs, and clinical text.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Knowledge-Guided Agentic AI: Synergizing Medical Standards, Ontologies, and Clinical Decision Support
sources.scope: Healthcare AI is shifting from predictive models to autonomous Agentic AI capable of complex reasoning and task execution. This Special Section focuses on the Informatics Core, moving beyond general LLMs to ensure clinical reliability in high-stakes environments.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Multimodal Edge-Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Digital Twins in Personalized Healthcare
sources.scope: Multimodal Edge-Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Digital Twins in Personalized Healthcare represents a transformative convergence of biomedical signal processing, artificial intelligence, and edge computing to redefine patient-centered healthcare.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Precision and Preventive Healthcare
sources.scope: This special issue explores the transformative potential of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in healthcare, focusing on how they integrate text, images, signals, and speech to enable precision medicine and preventive care.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Quantum Key Distribution for Secure Healthcare Information in 6G-Enabled Systems
sources.scope: The Special Issue on “Quantum Key Distribution for Secure Healthcare Information in 6G-Enabled Systems” explores the convergence of quantum communication and next-generation wireless technologies to address the growing security challenges in digital healthcare.

sources.journalTitle: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
sources.title: Quantum–Agentic Systems for Next-Generation Personalized and Predictive Healthcare
sources.scope: This special Issue on Quantum–Agentic Systems for Next-Generation Personalized and Predictive Healthcare will explore the fusion of Quantum Computing, Agentic Artificial Intelligence, and Bio-Digital Twin technologies to build the next generation of autonomous, intelligent, and personalized healthcare systems.

Short paper – 8 double column pages
Comments paper – 2 double column pages
Survey papers – 20 double column pages
A double column page is defined as a 7.875″ x 10.75″ page with 9.5-point type and 11.5-point vertical spacing.

sources.scope: For over 35 years and some 80-plus contributions, Gene Woolsey (former editor in chief of the INFORMS Journal on Applied Analytics) penned “The Fifth Column.” Today, IJAA is bringing back the “Fifth Column,” but with a submission process. sources.title: Call for papers: Conflict adaptation across single-task and multi-tasking paradigms
sources.scope: Over the last 30 years, cognitive-control research has extensively focused on conflict adaptation, namely the processes by which control mechanisms are up- or down-regulated depending on prior experiences of cognitive conflict (Botvinick et al., 2001; Braver 2012).
sources.requirements:
Over the last 30 years, cognitive-control research has extensively focused on conflict adaptation, namely the processes by which control mechanisms are up- or down-regulated depending on prior experiences of cognitive conflict (Botvinick et al., 2001; Braver 2012). As a result of these efforts, many signatures of conflict adaptation are now evidenced in both single-task (e.g., Stroop, flanker, Simon paradigms) and multi-tasking contexts (task-switching and dual tasking). Nonetheless, for a long time these effects have been studied in isolation within each paradigm.
Finally, the third question explores the relationship between the ability to stay focused on the task-relevant feature (i.e., cognitive stability) and the ability to switch between tasks (i.e., cognitive flexibility). These abilities have classically been assumed to trade off (Goschke, 2003; 2013), such that stability can only be augmented at the expenses of flexibility (and vice versa).

sources.title: Call for Papers | Journal of International Marketing | Artificial Intelligence in International Marketing: Mapping Impact Across the Domains of the Field
sources.scope: Artificial intelligence in international marketing sits at a similar kind of inflection point: It is foundational enough to reshape the field, still undertheorized to warrant sustained scholarly attention, and managerially urgent to justify JIM’s practitioner-facing mission.
sources.requirements: The current gap between the speedy evolution of AI and scholarly research is real and substantial, and is not limited to the export domain. At the same time, the window to claim this research avenue for JIM is narrowing.
sources.rawDateText:
Proposal Deadline: August 21, 2026
Article Submission Deadline: December 15, 2026
International marketing managers, export directors, global brand managers, and MNE strategy teams are making AI-related decisions right now, largely without the guidance of a systematic research base. Gartner (2025), for example, projects that by 2028, 90% of B2B buying will be intermediated by AI agents in one way or the other, channeling more than $15 trillion in spend through (semi-) automated agent-to-agent exchanges. Hence, the current practitioner stakes are immediate and substantial.
Models of sequential international marketing decisions—market entry timing, pricing adaptation, brand investment allocation—as a new theoretical and empirical approach to strategy under uncertainty.
AI agents as autonomous actors in global markets that reshape consumer decision-making, B2B procurement, brand management, and MNE governance, raising the need for new theoretical frameworks for markets in which intelligence is no longer exclusively human.
For illustration: does Hofstede’s power distance dimension still moderate brand evaluation when a consumer delegates product selection to an AI shopping agent? Do country-of-origin effects migrate from the purchase decision to the agent-programming decision? Is the Uppsala model’s core mechanism, gradual learning through experiential knowledge accumulation, disrupted when AI agents can synthesize market intelligence at machine speed? Questions like these run through every domain of international marketing, and we invite conceptual papers that engage them.

sources.dateText:
The Journal of Risk and Insurance (JRI) invites paper submissions for a planned special issue (or partial issue) on the topic of health insurer decision-making. While many studies analyze health insurance markets with a focus on decisions by individuals, healthcare providers, and policy-makers, this special issue will support the burgeoning literature investigating health insurer decision-making.
Topics of interest are broad and could include, for example, the ways that insurers respond to regulation, trends in the prevalence and nature of provider-sponsored health plans, decisions about horizontal mergers among insurers, insurer decisions about plan or network designs, and the operation of self-insured vs. fully insured health insurance plans. We are open to research on a range of health insurance markets and expressly encourage international comparisons and perspectives.
A special editorial team, consisting of Jean Abraham (University of Minnesota), Hanming Fang (University of Pennsylvania), Amanda Starc (Northwestern University), Justin Sydnor (University of Wisconsin-Madison), and Nicolas Ziebarth (Cornell University) will handle the papers for this submission. Papers will undergo the JRI’s standard peer-review process and the standards for acceptance will be the same as for other papers in the journal. Papers should be of general interest to the readership of the JRI, which is the leading journal specializing in risk management and insurance. The JRI is receptive to a range of methodological approaches, provided that they are appropriate for the research questions and analysis being undertaken. In particular, we are open to papers that are largely descriptive in nature but stress that these papers need to make a substantive contribution to our general understanding of the functioning of health insurance markets.

CLOSED
Special Issue on Health Insurer Decision-Making (CLOSED)

sources.dateText:
Editors of the Journal of the American Statistical Association are seeking papers for a special issue dedicated to exploring the intersection of statistical theory, methods, and applications with core problems in artificial intelligence, popularly called AI. This issue aims to map the evolving landscape of innovative statistical research inspired and motivated by the rapid developments in AI and pioneer integrated statistical AI methods to advance scientific discovery and trustworthy AI.
* Statistical Contributions to AI: The focus should be on how statistical theories and methodologies can offer unique insights into or solutions to the identified AI problems and empower AI methods and tools to advance real-world science. Contributions should be grounded in statistical rigor and demonstrate a clear link to addressing the AI challenges and their practical applications.
* Innovative Statistical AI Theory, Method, and Applications: Each submission should not only highlight the intersection of statistics and AI but also propose specific contributions to statistical theory, methodology, and application within the chosen area. This could include new statistical models, inventive analysis methods, novel approaches to existing statistical techniques, or innovative data analysis and statistical AI applications aimed at addressing real-world problems AI endeavors to solve.
* Innovative Statistical AI Theory, Method, and Applications: Each submission should not only highlight the intersection of statistics and AI but also propose specific contributions to statistical theory, methodology, and application within the chosen area. This could include new statistical models, inventive analysis methods, novel approaches to existing statistical techniques, or innovative data analysis and statistical AI applications aimed at addressing real-world problems AI endeavors to solve.

sources.title: Call for Papers: PSJ Special Issue on Policy Diffusion
sources.scope: The Policy Studies Journal (PSJ) invites submissions for a special Issue focusing on policy diffusion. Since Walker’s groundbreaking work 65 years ago, policy diffusion research has both burgeoned and stagnated at times (Mooney 2021).
sources.requirements: This special issue invites papers that engage on any of the four fronts listed above: data, methods, theory, and context. Importantly, the aim is not to publish studies of a single policy using conventional methods (e.g., Event History Analysis) that confirm existing theory. We are looking for work that continues to push the boundaries of policy diffusion research.
sources.dateText:
\*\*The deadline for submitting a manuscript for the Special Issue is December 1, 2025\*\*
Potential contributors to the Special Issue may participate in a “Peer Paper Exchange” in the spring of 2025, through which authors can obtain informal feedback from peers who also plan to submit a paper to the Special Issue and opt to participate in the Exchange. For the exchange, papers will be paired together so the authors can exchange and provide each other with feedback. It is not a formal workshop. Participation in the exchange is intended to support the development of papers but has no bearing on the peer review process that will be undertaken by PSJ once papers are submitted to the journal. That review process is formal and entirely independent of the Peer Paper Exchange.
To participate in the Peer Paper Exchange, please submit a one-page abstract that explains your research question, the contribution of your research to policy diffusion, and the data and methodological approaches you plan to use to answer your research question, along with the paper title and author information. This is due by April 1st. Notifications of acceptance to participate in the Peer Paper Exchange will be made by May 15th.
Authors participating in the Exchange must share their draft papers with fellow participants by September 1st. Comments from the Exchange review will be returned to the authors by October 1st.
* May 15, 2025: Decisions sent for inclusion in peer exchange
* December 1, 2025: Deadline for submitting to PSJ

Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Production Systems: Empirical Evidence, Implementation Pipelines, and Industrial Applications
sources.scope: Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Production Systems: Empirical Evidence, Implementation Pipelines, and Industrial Applications
sources.dateText:
Manuscript deadline
30 June 2027
Artificial Intelligence–Enabled Production Systems: Empirical Evidence, Implementation Pipelines, and Industrial Applications
Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly moving from a standalone “analytics tool” to an operational capability that reshapes how production systems are planned, controlled, and improved in real time. In production contexts, AI can be understood as digital technologies performing tasks and decisions traditionally associated with human intelligence (Pomerol, 1997).
Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly moving from a standalone “analytics tool” to an operational capability that reshapes how production systems are planned, controlled, and improved in real time. In production contexts, AI can be understood as digital technologies performing tasks and decisions traditionally associated with human intelligence (Pomerol, 1997).
As AI becomes embedded in industrial practice, it increasingly augments other production technologies by enabling learning-driven planning and control, data-driven quality and maintenance decisions, and closed-loop optimisation across cyber–physical production environments.
However, what remains underdeveloped is system-level, empirically validated knowledge on how these point solutions are integrated with production technologies and operational data environments to form reliable end-to-end decision-and-execution workflows that generalise beyond individual tasks or single settings (Smyth et al., 2024).
In practice, AI will not augment production technologies as expected unless implementation conditions are addressed across the relationships between business needs, data readiness, and AI-enabled decision workflows.
Before AI can be operationalised, organisations must clarify the business decision and process context, specify what data are needed for those decisions, and prepare usable production data through definition, collection, storage, integration, and cleaning—forming a foundational implementation pipeline that starts before AI model building (Mao et al., 2025).
Empirical studies may employ machine learning, optimisation, simulation, or digital twin experimentation, but only when the analysis is grounded in real operational data and/or validated in industrial settings with measurable outcomes (e.g., improvements in scheduling performance, quality, throughput, downtime, or decision accuracy).
In addition to application-focused empirical papers, we explicitly encourage submissions that examine the full AI implementation pipeline in production systems, including business–AI alignment, where production decision problems are translated into AI use cases and data requirements; data readiness, where governance/standards, monitoring, preparation/cleaning, and query/access enable reliable AI use; and deployment and workflow embedding, where AI outputs are integrated into human–AI decision workflows and operational routines.
While many emerging deployments take workflow-oriented or agent-like forms, an agentic framing is not required. Instead, we welcome any empirically grounded study that demonstrates how AI is operationalised across the production decision pipeline and linked to measurable production outcomes.
To improve coherence, we organise the Special Issue topics along two dimensions, as can be seen from Table 1: (i) stages of AI implementation in production systems—from business–AI alignment (design), to data readiness (pre-implementation), to deployment and workflow embedding (implementation); and (ii) the production technologies and operational contexts in which AI is used to augment decision-making and execution (e.g., cyber–physical systems/digital twins, additive manufacturing, blockchain-enabled data infrastructures).
Business–AI alignment (design) | Decision requirements for planning/control/quality; DT use-case definition | AM decision needs; customisation requirements; AM capacity/quality decision points | Traceability/audit needs; data products and access requirements
Table 1 provides a high-level map of the SI scope. Topic areas below offer illustrative (non-exhaustive) examples of suitable empirical submissions. Across these topics, we particularly welcome papers that examine how business needs are translated into AI design choices and production decision workflows, how data readiness conditions enable or constrain implementation, and how AI outputs are embedded into human–AI decision workflows in real production settings.
* AI-Augmented Production Planning and Control: studies that focus on predictive and prescriptive analytics empowered by AI for production planning, sequencing, scheduling, and dispatching; studies that explore reinforcement learning and autonomous decision-making for factory operations; studies that examine AI-supported capacity management, workflow optimisation, and constraint handling in real operational environments.
* Business–AI Alignment and AI Readiness Pipeline for Production Systems: empirical studies that examine how production decisions and business processes are translated into AI use cases and data requirements (i.e., what data are needed for what decisions); studies that investigate data governance/standards, data quality monitoring, data preparation, cleaning, integration, and query/access in production settings; studies that develop and empirically validate measures of AI readiness (e.g., data readiness, process readiness, organisational readiness) for AI-enabled production technologies.
* Agentic and Workflow-Oriented Deployment in Production: empirical studies that investigate how AI-enabled workflows connect data preparation, querying, and analysis to production decisions and execution (e.g., natural-language interfaces to databases/BI, AI-assisted reporting and decision support, and early forms of production “agents” that operationalise decision guidance); studies that evaluate operational performance impacts and human–AI interaction within such workflows.
* AI-Enabled Cyber–Physical Production Systems and Digital Twins: studies that develop and empirically assess intelligent digital twins for real-time optimisation, forecasting, and scenario evaluation; studies that investigate hybrid physics–AI approaches embedded within cyber–physical production environments; studies that provide evidence on continuous learning, data flow, and synchronisation between physical systems and their digital representations; studies that analyse AI-enabled control using real sensor/machine/robot data, including edge AI for decentralised and real-time decision-making; and studies that examine human–robot collaboration enhanced by AI-based perception, adaptive learning, and decision support tools.
* Human–AI Interaction and Organisational Transformation: studies that investigate human-in-the-loop AI and operator–AI collaboration in production environments; studies that examine how operators, engineers, and managers guide AI systems, interpret AI outputs, evaluate AI-generated recommendations, and decide whether to accept, adapt, or override AI-supported decisions; studies that document organisational readiness, capability development, skill transformation, and adoption challenges associated with AI-enabled production systems; studies that examine explainability, trust, transparency, and governance mechanisms influencing AI deployment on the factory floor.
* Empirical Innovations in Data, Measurement, and Evaluation: studies that utilise field experiments, industry datasets, IoT streams, digital twin logs, video analytics, or multimodal data to evaluate the performance and impact of AI-enabled production technologies; studies that demonstrate measurable improvements in productivity, quality, flexibility, or decision accuracy resulting from AI integration.
* Extended Production Contexts (Production-Adjacent Physical Operations): studies that examine AI embedded in production-adjacent execution systems where planning/control decisions are central, such as warehousing and fulfilment operations; studies that empirically evaluate AI-enabled AMRs for picking, transport, and sorting; studies that assess real-time slotting/routing, vision systems for object recognition and damage detection, and workforce–robot coordination, with explicit implications for operational control and performance.
Pomerol, J.C. (1997) ‘Artificial intelligence and human decision making’, European Journal of Operational Research, 99(1), pp. 3–25. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0377-2217(96)00378-5

sources.title: Bridging the Gap Between Artificial Intelligence and Risk Analysis: Human–AI Teaming Perspectives
sources.scope: Society has witnessed significant advances in the adoption of artificial intelligence and, more recently, generative AI systems. These developments increasingly enable human–AI teams to perform activities that were previously carried out by humans or AI alone.
sources.requirements: Submissions should explicitly engage with human–AI interaction, division of labor, workflow integration, or accountability in risk analysis. Papers that focus solely on AI methods for risk assessment, or solely on risks posed by AI systems themselves, are out of scope unless they directly analyze implications for human–AI teaming in risk-analytic practice.
sources.dateText:
Submission deadline: Saturday, 31 October 2026
Society has witnessed significant advances in the adoption of artificial intelligence and, more recently, generative AI systems. These developments increasingly enable human–AI teams to perform activities that were previously carried out by humans or AI alone. This transformation across society and industry requires a deeper understanding of how risk science can inform, guide, and govern risk assessment and decision-making when AI systems are embedded within human workflows.
This Special Issue focuses on human–AI teaming as the primary unit of analysis in risk assessment and risk-informed decision-making. Rather than examining how AI or machine learning can independently perform risk analysis, the emphasis is on how AI systems (including machine learning methods and large language models) function as collaborative agents within human-centered risk analysis processes, and on the implications of such teaming for risk science.
AI systems may be opaque or transparent depending on application context, time constraints, and design choices, with each offering distinct benefits and challenges. We therefore seek contributions that examine how risk can be characterized, communicated, validated, and governed when human judgment and AI systems jointly contribute to risk assessment outcomes.
Deadline for Manuscript Submission: October 31, 2026

sources.title: Polarization and Health Policy in a Global Context
sources.scope: Political polarization is on the rise in many parts of the world. Research shows that polarization has numerous negative impacts on population health (Fraser et al., 2022; Nayak et al., 2021; Oberlander, 2024). Rising political polarization often leads to polarization of health issues as well, such as vaccine or pandemic response policies.

sources.title: VSI: AI and Inequality
sources.scope: This special issue focuses on a critical but underexplored dimension of AI: its role in widening or narrowing social inequalities. As AI tools are rolled out across sectors like healthcare, education, long-term care and the labor market, their impacts are not distributed equally across race, class, gender, and other axes of social stratification.

sources.title: Agentic AI and the Future of Leadership: The Emergence of Leadership as a Service
sources.scope: The mid-2020s represent a structural inflection point in socio-technical evolution. We are witnessing a fundamental departure from ‘AI as a reactive tool’ to ‘Agentic AI’—autonomous systems characterized by goal-directed reasoning and iterative planning. This evolution has birthed a radical organizational paradigm: Leadership as a Service (LaaS).

sources.scope: This Special Issue examines how technological sovereignty is reshaping the design, governance, and objectives of innovation policies. sources.dateText:
West European Politics welcomes proposals for special issues. The Journal normally publishes two special issues per year. They are selected on a competitive basis. Full proposals for special issues should be submitted at least two years before planned publication. Proposals considered suitable by the editors will be reviewed prior to a decision being taken. All articles published in the Journal are subject to our double anonymous peer review system, with reviewers chosen by special issue editors in consultation with the editors of the journal. Decisions on publication will be taken on the basis of reviewers’ reports. An invitation to prepare a special issue does not constitute a guarantee of publication of either the special issue or of individual articles therein.
West European Politics welcomes proposals for symposia. A symposium is similar to a special issue, also guest edited but with fewer papers. Symposia may address a common empirical concern in the study of European politics, government or public policy; focus on conceptual or theoretical debates; discuss methodological advances; or engage with topical normative questions. Symposia comprise four to six articles, one of which may be an introductory article by the guest editors. They are selected on a competitive basis. All articles published in the journal are subject to double blind peer review, with reviewers chosen by the editors of the journal. Decisions on publication will be taken on the basis of reviewers’ reports. An invitation to prepare a symposium does not constitute a guarantee of publication of either the symposium or of individual articles therein.

sources.requirements:
一、年会征文的投稿、评审、录用
本届年会投稿分为摘要投稿及全文投稿，其中全文投稿将向学会下属期刊推荐，提供快速通道发表。只有通过会议系统在线提交，经过评审录用并注册才能进入会议程序。具体要求如下：
1. 在线投稿，网址为 sesc2024.casconf.cn。全文投稿需选择期望被推荐的期刊和主题。一般摘要投稿可选择主题。学会分支机构组织的分会场或专家组织的专题论坛的投稿一律视为摘要投稿，选择分会场和专题论坛名称即可。
2. 全文投稿和一般摘要投稿均由年会学术委员会组织评审。分会场或专题论坛的投稿由相应活动组织者负责。正式录取均由会议平台发送通知。
3. 中国系统工程学会下属全部期刊（包括：《系统工程理论与实践》、《系统工程学报》、《交通运输系统工程与信息》、《系统科学与系统工程学报》（英文版）和《系统科学与信息学报》（英文版）均参加全文推荐投稿。被推荐投稿后需注册会议，同时投稿期刊并遵守期刊全部要求（最终是否被期刊录取与年会无关）。后续有其他期刊加入，可直接从会议网站获悉。
sources.dateText:

关于征集“人工智能时代的审计（2026）”专题研讨会论文的通知
sources.scope:
一、征文内容
围绕人工智能技术发展的最新进展，立足审计面临的新要求新挑战新任务，研究人工智能时代审计理论框架、审计中运用人工智能技术所面临的审计风险、人工智能时代的审计取证、人工智能技术在审计领域的应用场景以及可能面临的法律问题等。鼓励计算机科学、法学、经济学等学科在人工智能审计领域的交叉研究，总结人工智能技术在审计中应用的最新进展，为人工智能时代审计的创新发展提供更多理论和实践支撑。征文选题包括但不限于以下方面：
1.人工智能时代的审计理论框架构建
2.人工智能时代的审计数据治理
3.审计中运用人工智能技术所面临的风险
4.运用人工智能技术获取的审计证据的可靠性与证明力
5.审计大模型的构建及应用
6.多模态审计数据智能融合分析
7.审计智能体的构建及应用
8.人工智能技术在审计领域的应用场景
9.应用人工智能技术开展审计风险评估和控制
10.基于人工智能技术的审计流程优化
11.人工智能时代审计制度创新与法律问题
12.人工智能伦理与审计责任
sources.requirements:
二、论文要求
（一）坚持正确的政治方向、价值取向和学术导向，遵守意识形态纪律和学术道德要求。
（二）坚持理论联系实际，论点鲜明，论据充分，论证严谨，对实践有指导意义。
（三）论文题目自拟，论文既可以针对某一相关问题开展深入细致的研究，也可以对人工智能时代审计的创新实践或解决方案进行描述展示，实践总结要有应用实例支撑。
（四）论文内容须为原创且未公开发表，符合保密规定，所有引用文献应注明出处。
（五）论文字数限在10000字以内，以小四号宋体WORD排版，要有摘要、关键词、正文和参考文献（按著者—出版年制编排），如有注释均在当页脚注。
（六）论文题目下方需标明作者姓名、单位和手机号码。
三、论文提交与成果运用
（一）提交论文的截止时间为2026年4月27日。请发送论文电子版至电子邮箱xuehuihzkt@sina.com，文件名和邮件主题栏均为“单位+作者+手机号码+人工智能征文+论文题目”。
（二）经专家评审遴选出优秀论文，邀请优秀论文作者参加专题研讨会作成果交流。
（三）优秀论文将集结成册，并择优推荐在《审计研究》杂志刊发。
sources.dateText: （一）提交论文的截止时间为2026年4月27日。

一、年会征文的投稿、评审、录用

1. 在线投稿，网址为 sesc2024.casconf.cn。全文投稿需选择期望被推荐的期刊和主题。一般摘要投稿可选择主题。学会分支机构组织的分会场或专家组织的专题论坛的投稿一律视为摘要投稿，选择分会场和专题论坛名称即可。
2. 全文投稿和一般摘要投稿均由年会学术委员会组织评审。分会场或专题论坛的投稿由相应活动组织者负责。正式录取均由会议平台发送通知。

sources.title: “人工智能在系统科学中的运用”专题论文工作坊征稿通知
sources.scope:
一、专题背景与征稿方向
随着人工智能技术的迅猛发展，系统科学正面临着从“模型驱动”向“数据与智能驱动”范式转型的重大机遇。如何利用AI理解复杂系统的演化机理、优化系统决策、解决管理科学中的瓶颈问题，已成为当前学界与业界共同关注的焦点。
为促进AI与系统科学的深度融合，推动管理科学与数据科学的交叉创新，《系统科学与数学》期刊特推出“人工智能在系统科学中的运用”专题论文工作坊。旨在汇聚全国专家学者，围绕AI赋能复杂系统建模、大数据环境下的管理决策、智能算法的鲁棒性与伦理边界等前沿议题，展开深入研讨。
特邀征稿方向包括但不限于：
面向复杂系统的数据挖掘与机器学习方法
商务智能、电子商务中的AI算法与应用
AI系统的伦理风险、公平性及可信性研究
基于大数据的社会治理、智慧城市与金融科技
推荐系统、个性化算法与用户行为分析
系统科学视角下的AI使能与治理框架
sources.requirements:
三、投稿与评审说明
投稿要求：稿件需为原创学术论文，未在国内外公开发行的刊物或会议上发表或宣读过。论文需具有明确的创新性、科学性及与应用价值。
投稿方式：请将论文全文Word版发送至专用邮箱：scopehe@163.com； xtkx@amss.ac.cn。邮件主题及稿件命名格式务必为：“AI系统科学专题+作者姓名”。
截稿日期：2026年6月30日（以邮件发送时间为准）。
四、入选论文交流与推荐
入围本专题的优秀稿件，将有机会受邀参加线下深度交流：
工作坊交流：优秀论文作者将受邀参加2026年8月21-23日于北京石油化工学院举行的专题论文工作坊，进行现场汇报，与特邀专家及同行面对面交流。
论坛联动：该工作坊是“2026年高校管理学院/公共管理学院院长论坛暨中国双法研究会高等教育管理分会学术年会”重要组成部分。与会论文将在此学术年会上进行集中展示。
推荐意见：工作坊将组织专家对现场交流的论文进行点评与评议，最终根据质量与创新性给出《系统科学与数学》期刊的推荐意见，优先进入期刊正式审稿流程。
投稿咨询邮箱：scopehe@163.com； xtkx@amss.ac.cn。
sources.dateText: 截稿日期：2026年6月30日（以邮件发送时间为准）。

sources.scope:
二、投稿范围
围绕“低空制造产业创新生态、商业模式与场景驱动”，采用建模分析、实证研究、案例剖析、仿真模拟等研究方法，主题包括（但不限于）以下领域：
1. 低空装备制造关键核心技术突破与创新路径研究
2. 低空制造工艺创新、柔性生产与智能化制造模式
3. 低空装备模块化设计、平台化开发与货架化适配机制
4. 面向低空制造的数字孪生、工业互联网与智能工厂管理
5. 低空制造产业创新生态系统的多主体协同与演化机制
6. 低空制造产业金融—供应—运维—生态四链融合与治理
7. 低空制造产业可持续投融资模式与价值创造机制
8. 面向自主可控的低空供应链安全评估与协同决策
9. 低空装备全生命周期运维保障体系与健康智能管理
10. 低空运输服务需求生成机理与高价值场景识别
11. 低空商业模式演化中的规模经济、范围经济与网络效应
12. 低空制造企业的平台化转型与生态化商业模式设计
13. 低空空域产权配置、路权定价与多主体权益协同治理
14.
sources.requirements:
四、征文要求
来稿应为尚未发表的原创成果；格式参考《系统管理学报》投稿要求；来稿字数不应低于八千字，以一万至一万五千字为宜。
五、组织形式
本次工作坊将邀请专家对投稿论文进行匿名评审，拟遴选出多篇论文，入选作者将获邀参会。工作坊会议期间，投稿作者宣讲论文，特邀专家点评指导。
六、工作坊议程
本次工作坊依托第四届空天系统管理创新发展论坛，预计以线下会议形式举行（地点及时间待定）。工作坊将开展分组论文宣讲，每篇论文报告15分钟，专家点评10分钟。工作坊结束后，经过客座编委评选，推荐优秀论文获得《系统管理学报》快速审稿资格。
七、论文发表
针对获得快速审稿资格的论文，经作者修改后，送《系统管理学报》外部专家审稿。若达到《系统管理学报》要求，将优先正刊发表。
八、相关说明
参会论文的优先采编权将归《系统管理学报》期刊所有，存在版权争议的论文请勿投稿。
九、投稿方式
投稿邮箱：lowalt_logistics@126.com，邮件题目请注明：“工作坊+论文题目+单位+姓名”。工作坊编委会收到投稿后会回复邮件确认收稿。

截至2026年7月30日。

sources.requirements:
征文要求
征文应为尚未公开发表且符合国际学术规范的原创性研究成果。中文写作请参照《金融学季刊》体例，英文写作请参照Journal of Finance体例。作者信息（姓名、工作单位、通讯作者、联系电话、电子信箱等）请列于与正文独立的首页，其余部分均不能出现任何作者信息。
征文提交
作者请于2026年6月1日前将征文电子版（DOC或PDF格式）上传至：
https://wj.sysu.edu.cn/q/4Vf3Qeye
或扫描下方二维码提交。
论文评审
论坛将组建评审委员会对全部征文进行评审。论文入选通知及论坛邀请函将于2026年6月15日前向作者发出。
入选论文作者将受邀在本届论坛作现场报告（拟安排在7月12日星期日），每篇论文将由同行优秀学者作现场评议。其中的优秀论文经《金融学季刊》编辑部审定及作者同意后，可进入《金融学季刊》匿名审稿流程。

二、学术研讨议题包括（但不限于）：
1.构建中国金融学自主知识体系、走好中国特色金融发展之路研究
2.中央银行制度完善与货币政策传导机制优化研究
3.金融稳定、系统性风险防范与宏观审慎政策研究
4.金融改革、高水平开放与风险防控研究
5.存量经济学与国家资产负债表管理研究
6.金融支持扩大内需与消费升级研究
7.资本市场功能完善与高质量发展研究
8.耐心资本培育壮大与金融支持新质生产力研究
9.科技型中小企业全生命周期融资体系构建与风险分担机制研究
10.普惠金融风险定价、成本分担与商业可持续性研究
11.多层次、多支柱养老保险体系与养老金融高质量发展研究
12.中小金融机构改革化险与区域金融稳定研究
13.人工智能与金融融合发展研究
14.人民币国际化与国际金融体系改革研究
15.地缘政治与国际金融市场研究
16.跨境资本流动、汇率波动与金融安全屏障构建研究
sources.requirements:
三、投稿要求
投稿论文应为作者原创、未公开发表、无知识产权争议并应符合学术规范。论文应包括中英文标题、300字左右的中英文摘要、3-5个关键词、JEL分类号、正文、参考文献和作者信息。论文字数以2万字左右为宜，写作体例请参考《金融研究》网站（http://www.jryj.org.cn/）有关要求。为便于匿名评审，请将全部作者信息放在文章首页，其余部分均不能出现任何作者信息。请于2026年8月31日前投稿至邮箱cec_001@zju.edu.cn（Word和PDF两种格式文件均需上传,文件名为“作者姓名_论文标题”）。邮件主题格式为“2026《金融研究》论坛征文_作者姓名_论文标题”。
会议主办方将组织评审委员会对征文进行匿名评审，选出30篇左右入选论文。论文入选通知将于2026年9月20日前发出。入选论文作者将应邀参加第十七届《金融研究》论坛并在论坛相关分会场上宣读论文，主办方将邀请知名专家学者参加会议并对入选论文进行现场评议。经过论坛现场评议并按意见做出修改的论文，经作者同意，可直接进入《金融研究》发文匿名评审环节。《金融研究》论坛不收取任何费用，参会人员交通费和食宿费请自理。
详情亦可参阅《金融研究》网站（www.jryj.org.cn）；浙江大学经济学院网站（http://www.cec.zju.edu.cn）；浙江大学金融研究院网站（http://www.afr.zju.edu.cn）。
